analogyReview.scope: All 11 current callouts plus surrounding technical claims and all 27 omissions independently reviewed. Familiar scenario, mapping, explicit limit and closed-panel answerability checked.

rel-fanout-gray-faults.label: an open shop with an unusable till
rel-fanout-gray-faults.rationale: An open door resembles a shallow health check; a completed purchase resembles the useful operation whose latency matters. Limit: A service can fail differently for different callers. Measure real request paths rather than replacing one shallow check with another.

rel-wrong-answers-hidden-dependencies.rationale: Wrong-answer and shared-dependency examples are more direct than another comparison.

rel-cells-shuffle-isolation.label: separate buildings with a shared entrance map
rel-cells-shuffle-isolation.rationale: Each building corresponds to a cell serving its assigned customers; the shared map corresponds to the cell router. Limit: Software faults can cross intended boundaries through shared dependencies or retries. Isolation must be designed and tested, not assumed from a diagram.

rel-survivor-capacity-static-stability.rationale: The three-node survivor example already makes redistribution concrete.

rel-correlated-failure-review.rationale: Shared release and shared dependency examples directly expose correlation.

rel-latency-timeouts-deadlines.label: one lunch break for several errands
rel-latency-timeouts-deadlines.rationale: The lunch break is the whole-operation budget; each call and wait spends part of the same remaining time. Limit: A deadline cannot reverse work already done. Services must observe cancellation, and timing behaviour depends on the runtime.

rel-write-retry-safety.rationale: Payment retry and retention are already familiar concrete operations.

rel-backoff-jitter-distribution.label: staggering departures after an event
rel-backoff-jitter-distribution.rationale: Varied departure times map to random retry delays; identical schedules map to repeated synchronised waves. Limit: Spreading arrivals does not create capacity or limit the total number of attempts. Retries still require safety, deadlines and budgets.

rel-jitter-variants-sdk-policy.rationale: The distribution comparison and timing bounds are clearer than an added metaphor.

rel-retry-layer-amplification.rationale: The nested service diagram directly represents multiplication.

rel-retry-quota-deadline-loop.rationale: Native quota events and the call loop are the useful representation.

rel-queue-latency-tails.rationale: The explicit queue and utilisation table already ground the model.

rel-inflight-work-bulkhead-pools.label: watertight compartments in a ship
rel-inflight-work-bulkhead-pools.rationale: A bounded resource pool confines the slots a troubled dependency can occupy, preserving other pools. Limit: Shared memory, CPUs or other dependencies can still transmit the failure. Separating one pool does not isolate the whole process.

rel-breaker-recovery-static-fallbacks.rationale: The named breaker state machine and fallback table are sufficient.

rel-admission-goodput-priority.rationale: The admission code and priority examples expose the mechanism directly.

rel-adaptive-throttle-bounded-flow.rationale: Bounded queues and producer signals are already concrete.

rel-recovery-targets-isolated-backups.label: a copied notebook and an older saved edition
rel-recovery-targets-isolated-backups.rationale: Current copies map to replication; independently retained history maps to backup and point-in-time recovery. Limit: The recovered edition may lack later valid changes. Storage isolation, usable keys, log continuity and restore testing decide what actually survives.

rel-dr-strategy-coordination-cost.rationale: The strategy spectrum directly compares provisioning and coordination.

rel-regional-failover-fencing-lag.rationale: The failover checklist is more useful than a second recovery analogy.

rel-chaos-hypotheses-game-days.rationale: The controlled experiment specification supplies the real scenario.

rel-metric-cardinality-histograms.rationale: Metric label and bucket examples directly show costs and aggregation.

rel-structured-log-cost-context.rationale: The same event in text, JSON and SQL is the clearest comparison.

rel-trace-context-tail-collection.label: a parcel reference carried through depots
rel-trace-context-tail-collection.rationale: Carried trace context connects observations across services; spans record the separate stages. Limit: Requests can branch, overlap or link to separate traces, and sampling can omit observations. A trace is not automatically a complete record.

rel-red-use-actionable-alerts.rationale: RED/USE checklists already distinguish service symptoms and resource causes.

rel-user-journey-sli-contracts.rationale: The concrete checkout SLI supplies the needed example.

rel-error-budget-policy-burn.label: a spending allowance with agreed rules
rel-error-budget-policy-burn.rationale: The error budget is an allowed level of bad outcomes; the pre-agreed policy turns its use into release and reliability decisions. Limit: User failures are not desirable purchases. Traffic and rolling history change the accounting, and spending budget never waives safety or security obligations.

rel-burn-alert-threshold-selection.rationale: The operational threshold table is clearer than an analogy.

rel-multiwindow-alert-detection.rationale: The policy code directly illustrates long/short-window logic.

rel-low-volume-slo-review.rationale: The quiet-service event example directly shows unstable ratios.

rel-rolling-blue-green-cutover.rationale: Deployment diagrams directly represent the two routing shapes.

rel-canary-evidence-rollout-waves.label: trying a new recipe on a small batch
rel-canary-evidence-rollout-waves.rationale: The batch maps to limited release exposure; representative sampling and waiting map to canary evidence and bake time. Limit: Production cohorts can differ, and failures can be correlated or delayed. A successful sample does not prove the whole release safe.

rel-feature-flags-reader-first.rationale: The native flag fragment and reader-first sequence are already concrete.

rel-expand-contract-lock-safe.rationale: The column migration and lock queue are practical examples.

rel-transport-storage-security-limits.rationale: The layered diagram directly places controls against threats.

rel-envelope-keys-rotation-erasure.label: a locked box with a separately protected key
rel-envelope-keys-rotation-erasure.rationale: The data key encrypts the bulk contents; the wrapping key protects the stored data-key copy. Limit: Cryptographic formats need nonce and integrity protections. Cached or copied plaintext keys can bypass the key service, and rotating a wrapping key is not erasing old data.

rel-identity-secrets-zero-trust.rationale: Resource authorisation maps to individual room permissions; physical location cannot establish trust and identity/context checks continue.

rel-owasp-2025-safe-denial.rationale: The risk/control table and authorisation timeout are direct.

rel-ddos-edge-amplification.rationale: The reflected-packet mechanism is concrete without another comparison.
